interpretations: For each nonmissing event name, average the nonmissing `budget.amount` values from budget lines joined to matching events. Keep names whose average exceeds the unweighted mean of those per-name averages. Show the name, its average, the difference from that mean, and its average divided by that mean, without rounding

Include events with a missing event name as one group. If that group has a nonmissing average budgeted amount above the mean of the per-name averages, show it with the same calculations and no rounding
queries:
WITH name_averages AS (
    SELECT e.event_name, AVG(b.amount) AS average_amount
    FROM event AS e
    JOIN budget AS b ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id
    WHERE e.event_name IS NOT NULL
      AND b.amount IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY e.event_name
),
overall_mean AS (
    SELECT AVG(average_amount) AS mean_amount
    FROM name_averages
)
SELECT n.event_name,
       n.average_amount,
       n.average_amount - m.mean_amount AS difference_from_mean,
       n.average_amount / m.mean_amount AS ratio_to_mean
FROM name_averages AS n
CROSS JOIN overall_mean AS m
WHERE n.average_amount > m.mean_amount

WITH per_name AS (
    SELECT e.event_name,
           AVG(b.amount) AS average_budgeted_amount
    FROM event AS e
    LEFT JOIN budget AS b
        ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id
    GROUP BY e.event_name
)
SELECT event_name, average_budgeted_amount
FROM per_name
WHERE average_budgeted_amount > (
    SELECT AVG(average_budgeted_amount)
    FROM per_name
)
